instructions: On the weekend, or up to 5 days ahead: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Set 12 paper baking cups in a muffin pan. Take the butter and eggs out so they come up to room temperature.
Beat the butter and sugar with a mixer for 5 to 7 minutes, until pale and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating until each one is mixed in before the next.
Zest the lemon into the bowl. Stir in the honey and the vanilla.
Sift the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt together into a second bowl. Do it twice.
Fold the flour into the batter in three additions with a large spoon. Stop when no streaks are left, so the batter stays light.
Spoon the batter into the cups, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the tops are golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Let them sit in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.
Once they're cool, keep the sobaos in a zip bag at room temperature for up to 5 days. They're best from the second day. For the freezer, wrap each one and freeze for up to 2 months.
Thaw a frozen one on the counter. To warm any of them, microwave for 10 seconds.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the whole batch on the weekend, or up to 5 days ahead; they're best the day after baking.
method_notes: None of the three versions read shows a full set of ratings, so this leads with The Spanish Chef (4.8, no count shown). All use equal weights of butter, sugar and flour with eggs and a raising agent. The Spanish Chef uses baking powder, honey, lemon zest and vanilla; spain.info uses powdered yeast and rum and bakes at a similar heat, and Bake Street fills 6 big molds. Storage comes from Bake Street (best on day two, tender for about 5 days).
